notes: Both reviews caught the same two core concerns: (1) the Shift-state distilled-knowledge concern -- using GetAsyncKeyState's real-time physical Shift as a navigation fallback can misread uppercase/held Shift as backward navigation (GT0); and (2) the non-interactive horizontal scrollbar (Auto + IsHitTestVisible=False) concern (GT2/7/12/14). The DECISIVE difference is the off-screen-positioning distilled-knowledge concern: baseline #10 explicitly stated the magic -1000 parking offset 'could be insufficient for very large negative virtual-screen origins,' cleanly matching GT1/GT5/GT9; candidate #11 touched the exact same parking code but framed it only as a DIP-vs-physical coordinate-space mismatch, never arguing the offset could be too small, so it does not capture the specific insufficiency concern under strict matching. Neither review recovered the CsWin32 Directory.Packages.props blast-radius concern (GT4/10/13/15) -- candidate #14 discussed the UI.csproj PackageReference (missing Version) rather than the repo-wide bump; baseline never referenced Directory.Packages.props. Neither caught the stale characterName.Text when _selectedIndex==-1 (GT3/8; baseline #16 discussed index desync, a different concern) nor the unused-parameter rename (GT6/11). Both reviews are broad and raised many valid concerns outside the ground truth (DPI unit paths, SizeChanged jitter, MinWidth=600 conflicts), but on ground-truth recall baseline led purely by additionally nailing the off-screen offset insufficiency. Net: distilled-knowledge concerns helped both on shift-state and scrollbar; off-screen positioning helped baseline specifically; DPI and scrollbar-interactivity nuances were raised by both but DPI wasn't a ground-truth concern.
